To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the adsorption of pesticides on carbon cloth is a fast process and the order of the adsorption extent of the studied pesticides was metribuzin<2,4-D<bromacil<atrazine.
the removal of metribuzuin, bromacill, 2, 4-D and atrazin from water by adsorpion on high area carbon cloths was studied.
the extent of adsorption on high-area carbon cloth follows the order metribuzin<2,4-D<bromacil<atrazine, and the adsorption process follows a first-order kinetics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the removal of pesticides such atrazine, 2, 4-D and bromacil from water by adsorbing them onto high area carbon cloth.
the development of a new method for removal of pesticides from aqueous solutions by adsorption on carbon cloth and the kinetics of the process.
the development of a new method of removal of pesticides from aqueous solutions.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the adsorption process of metribuzil, bromacil and 2,4- D on carbon cloth is a fast process, while the adsorption of atrazine is slow and it is a first-order process for the adsorption of all pesticides studied.

the adsorption process of metribuzil, bromacil and 2,4D is mainly governed by the hydrophobic interactions between the carbon cloth and these pesticides, whereas the adsorption of atrazine is governed by a combination of hydrophobic and hydrogen bonding interactions between the carbon-cloth and the pesticide.
the adsorption process of the pesticides studied on the high area carbon cloth is a rapid process and the adsorbate-adsorbent interaction is strong.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
adsorption of pesticides on high area carbon cloths can be considered as a viable option for the removal of pesticides from water.
the adsorption process was rapid and the rate constants for the adsorption of metribuzine, 2, 4-D, bromacil and atrazine were determined.
the adsorption of pesticides from aqueous solutions is a feasible process for the removal of these pollutants from water.

high area carbon cloth can serve as a useful adsorbent for the removal of pesticides from water.
the adsorption of pesticides on carbon cloth can be effectively monitored by UV-spectroscopic technique in situ.
the carbon cloth has the potential to remove pesticides from water.
